cycles.name: Steel Breath
focuses: Turn the breathing envelope into a trained skill, audible exhale and honest RPE 7, and set every strength baseline submaximally on trunk-supported, fixed-path patterns.
Rebuild knee-flexion tolerance from a deliberately shallow range, and start prophylactic wrist-extensor loading before the elbow asks for it.
Film the top set of the hip thrust and the row every week, weigh in on a fixed morning, and get the doctor's answers in writing by 27 September.

paragraphs: You've been training five days a week and playing three or four on top of that, with under a year in the gym. That's a lot of work going into a body that's only getting so much sleep. We're going to three gym days, and every one of them has a job.

This block is about two things. Learning to breathe through hard work instead of holding your breath, and finding out what you can actually lift. Nobody knows your numbers yet, including you. Week two we find them properly, without ever going to failure.
Your knee and your elbow both get looked after here, not avoided. We load them in the range they can handle right now and we build from there.
outcomes: Every lift stopped 3 reps short, every rep breathing out
Real starting numbers on all four main lifts
Rear knee dropping to the same depth pain free, five weeks running
3 gym days a week held, no extras
Top set of the hip thrust and the row filmed every week
Weekly weigh-in sent, and the doctor's answers in writing by 27 September

cycles.name: Cold Forge
focuses: Move real strength inside the same RPE 7 cap by adding sets and breaking the heaviest work into clusters, so tension per rep rises while proximity to failure never does.
Extend knee range and single-leg load only as tolerance is proven, with slow eccentrics carrying the stimulus the load ceiling will not.

paragraphs: Cold Forge is where the weight starts moving properly. Same ceiling, same breathing, but we break the heavy work into pieces so you can lift more without ever grinding a rep.
You don't get there by pushing harder in this block. You get there by proving you can stop short every time.
teaser.hook: Earn the ceiling and I'll raise the floor.

cycles.name: Uncoil
focuses: Convert the strength into on-court speed through unloaded elastic and rotational work, the one quality the training ceiling does not touch at all.
Hold and re-measure the standards submaximally, and buy density only where the demand is aerobic rather than mechanical.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Use the machine if your gym has one. If you use a barbell, it gets loaded and unloaded on blocks and somebody else puts the plates on, you don't pick anything up off the floor. Do two build up sets first, about half your working weight for 5 then about three quarters for 3, then your 3 real sets. Film your top set.

Working glute burning, front of the hip long at the top

chips.label: breathe out on the way up

exercises.note: Dumbbells come off a rack at hip height, never off the floor. Your rear knee comes down to the mat stack and stops there. Straps on so your grip never limits you. If the knee complains, swap to a Box Step-Up on a box no higher than mid shin, start lighter and let RPE 7 find the weight.

exercises.name: Machine Seated Leg Curl
exercises.note: Curl to about ninety degrees and stop, you don't need to touch your backside. Set the machine's range limiter if it has one. Same reason as your leg extension, a swollen knee doesn't like the last part of the range. We open it up when the knee has settled.

exercises.name: Wrist Extension
exercises.note: Alternate arms with no rest in between, one arm's set is the other arm's rest. Dumbbells sitting on the bench before you start. Hold it loose in your fingers and let your hand open at the bottom of every rep. Count out loud the whole way through.

cards.title: If Your Heart Talks, Stop
cards.body:
You told me about your heart, and I'm glad you did. This program is built around it. But I want you to know exactly what to do if something happens while you're training.

Stop the session, sit down, and don't drive if you get any of these:

  • Pain, pressure or tightness in your chest
  • A racing, thumping or irregular heartbeat, even resting between sets
  • Feeling lightheaded, vision going grey, or like you might pass out
  • Breathing much harder than the work should make you
  • New pain going into your jaw, neck or arm
  • A cold sweat

If any of that happens, see a doctor the same day and message me before your next session. I'd rather you stop ten times for nothing than push through once.

You'll notice there are no heart rate targets anywhere in your program. That's on purpose. I don't know what medication you're on, so your heart rate isn't a number I can read for you.

cards.title: What I Need From Your Doctor
cards.body:
Right now I'm coaching you around a heart condition I only know one sentence about. That's not good enough for either of us, and it's the reason your program is careful in places it might not need to be.

Get me four things in writing from your doctor. What the condition is called. Whether you're cleared for weight training. Any blood pressure or heart rate limit. Whether you're on medication.

I need this before 27 September. If it hasn't come by then, I'll write to your doctor myself. Ask about the leg press and the belt squat while you're there, both of those could open up a lot for you.

cards.title: When Something Hurts
cards.body:
You've got three things we're managing. Your knee, your elbow, and your heart. Here's what to do when any of them speaks up.

Normal and fine: muscles burning during a set, feeling tired after, stiff the next morning. Keep training.

Not fine: sharp pain, anything shooting down your arm or leg, pins and needles, or pain that builds through a set instead of staying the same.

  • Mild and fading: finish the set and write it in your log
  • Building, or changing how you move: stop that exercise, use the swap on the card, message me
  • Sharp, shooting, numb or just weird: stop the session and message me before the next one

Telling me something hurts gets you a different exercise, not a rest day and not a lecture. I've built swaps into your cards already. Nothing you report takes training away from you.

cards.title: How To Pick Your Weight
cards.body:
The app never tells you what weight to use. You find it every time, and here's how.

On a new movement, start lighter than you think. Do the first set and ask yourself how many more you could have done. If the answer is more than three, go up next set. If it's less than three, come down.

RPE 7 means you rack it with 3 reps still in you. Not one, not two. Three. If a set felt like you only had one or two left, that was too heavy, take weight off for the next one.

Going down is not failing. Bad sleep, hard match the day before, stressful week, all of it makes the same weight feel heavier. Dropping the weight on those days is you reading yourself right, not you going backwards.

cards.title: Never Hold Your Breath
cards.body:
This is the most important thing in your whole program, and it's the reason the block is called Steel Breath.

Breathe out through the hard part of every single rep. Not after. During. On the way up out of the lunge, on the way up on the hip thrust, as you press the dumbbells.

Here's your check, and you can do it on your own without me watching. On the last two reps of any set, say a word out loud. If you can't get a word out, you were holding your breath or the weight was too heavy. Either way, take some off.

You'll also notice there's no belt in your program and there won't be one for a while. Same reason.

cards.title: Film These Two, Every Week
cards.body:
Two lifts get filmed every week. Your top set of the Single-Leg Hip Thrust on Day 1, and your top set of the Single-Arm Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row on Day 3.

Film from the side, with sound on. The sound matters as much as the picture, because I'm watching your breathing and your face as much as your technique.

Send them on WhatsApp the same day. The weight goes up on those two lifts after I've seen the film and cleared it. If the videos stop coming, the weight stops moving. That's not me being strict, it's the only way I can coach you properly when I'm not standing next to you.

cards.title: Week 2 Is Measuring Week
cards.body:
Week 1 you go light on everything. Treat it as learning the movements, nothing else. Keep every set easy.

Week 2 we find your real numbers. On the hip thrust, the row, the lunge and the wrist work, you add a small amount each set until the set hits RPE 7, or until the first rep slows down. Then you stop. That set is your number.

This is not a max and there's no last hard rep. Normally I'd have an athlete push a set to the limit to find this out. We're not doing that with you, and the reason is your heart. We get the same information by walking up to it instead of running into it.

cards.title: Your Knee Sets Its Own Depth
cards.body:
On the reverse lunge, your rear knee comes down to a stack of mats. That stack is your depth, and only I move it.

The mats come down one level after three clean sessions in a row. Clean means three things. No knee pain during it. No ache that evening. Kneecap no more puffy or warm the next morning than the day before.

If the knee is puffier or warmer in the morning, the mats go straight back up and you tell me. That's information, not a step backwards.

Realistically you might get one drop in this whole block, maybe none. That's fine and it's expected. In this cycle the weight goes up at the same depth. Depth comes later.

cards.title: The Forearm Work Is Not Optional
cards.body:
Your tennis elbow is gone. It comes back for a lot of players, and the best thing we know for stopping that is loading the muscles on top of your forearm slowly and regularly. That's the wrist work on Day 1 and Day 3.

If a session runs long, that is the last thing you cut. Before the bike, before the core, before anything. Skip the last exercise instead.

Two things while you do it. Hold the dumbbell loose in your fingers, not squeezed in a fist, and let your hand open at the bottom of each rep. And count out loud through the set. If you can't count out loud, it's too heavy.

You'll also see straps on every pulling exercise. That's the same protection. Your back should be what stops the set, never your grip.

cards.title: The Fourth Gym Day Costs You Tennis
cards.body:
You were doing five gym days plus three or four on court. I know three is going to feel like not enough, especially in the first couple of weeks. So let me tell you exactly what happens if you add days back.

The extra gym days don't get paid for by the gym. They get paid for by your tennis. And the bill turns up in three to five weeks, not thirteen.

What goes first is your repeat sprint and your change of direction. In practice that's the last step to a wide ball, and speed on your second serve. Then the knee starts talking. Then the elbow. And the trap is that it feels like you need more gym, so you add more.

Three days. If you finish a session and you've got more in you, that's the program working, not the program being too easy.

cards.title: When Gym Lands On A Tennis Day
cards.body:
Most of your gym days are going to be tennis days too. Here's the rule.

  • Gym after tennis, or leave at least 4 to 6 hours between them
  • If you can't get that gap, do the first main lift only and keep it at RPE 6
  • You can move the days around your tennis however you need, the order in the app is just the best version

On Day 2, if you're short on time, the bike is the part that matters. That's the one to keep.

cards.title: Eat Like You Train
cards.body:
You said your eating is average and inconsistent, and your sleep is a 5 out of 10. Those two are doing more damage to your training than anything in your program.

Protein at every meal, three times a day, roughly a palm and a half of something like chicken, meat, fish, eggs or dairy. That's the floor. Don't count anything yet, just don't skip it.

Weigh yourself once a week, same morning, same conditions, and send me the number. If your weight starts dropping while your lifts are stuck, that's a food problem and not a training problem, and I want to catch it early.

On sleep, we'll work on it. But even getting the 7 to 8 hours you're already getting to feel better quality is worth more to you than a fourth gym day.
